plans.note: Cap is mutual at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 with Excluded Claims defined in 21.3; check cap adequacy against annual spend (sec-2.1 commits USD 2M/yr) and confirm data/security, confidentiality and indemnity carve-outs are uncapped rather than merely excluded from 21.1/21.2.

No Section 20 appears in the outline even though sec-9.3 cross-references 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' and sec-21.3 assumes indemnification obligations exist; Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity appears to be missing and must be inserted, with any Customer indemnity kept narrow.
sec-12.4-2 imposes a 24-month worldwide non-compete on Customer, which we reject outright; it also contradicts sec-12.3's acknowledgement that Customer gave no non-compete commitment.

sec-7.2 (first instance) forces disclosure and match before engaging another provider, operating as de facto exclusivity; conflicts with sec-12.3's supplier-freedom language and compounds the sec-2.1 take-or-pay.
sec-7.2 is a reverse MFN running against us (we must surface and match third-party offers); direction is wrong and should be deleted, with sec-12.3's no-MFN acknowledgement retained.

sec-12.4 bars soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee for 24 months 'regardless of how the employee applies'; needs narrowing to 12 months, personnel actually engaged, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out consistent with sec-12.3.

Section 9 jumps from 9.3 to 9.5 and contains only cause-based rights; no Customer termination for convenience appears, and sec-2.1 expressly negates termination rights. Add a Customer convenience right on notice without penalty while confirming Vendor has no mid-term walk-away.

sec-8.2 auto-renews for 12 months with a 30-day opt-out plus a 60-day reminder and deadline extension; sec-8.3 caps uplifts at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Verify the notice window and uplift cap are acceptable and that non-renewal notice mechanics align with sec-29 notice requirements.

Direct conflict: sec-28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction while sec-28.2 gives New York County courts exclusive jurisdiction. Resolve to New York law and New York courts and delete the Singapore clause; sec-28.3 escalation is acceptable.

sec-24.1 permits our Affiliate/successor assignment, sec-24.2 restricts Vendor, and sec-24.4 blocks Vendor termination or repricing on our change of control; check sec-24.3's residual consent requirement does not swallow sec-24.1 and that sec-13.3 licence transfer tracks Section 24.

sec-14.2 wrongly gives Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables with only a revocable, non-transferable term licence to us — reverse to Customer ownership of paid-for Deliverables (or at minimum the perpetual sec-13.2 licence); sec-14.1 and sec-15.1 correctly keep Customer Data with us.

sec-13.1/13.2 cover Affiliates and contractors and grant a perpetual paid-up licence, and sec-13.3 limits revocation; the revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence in sec-14.2 is inconsistent and must be conformed.

sec-22.1–22.3 already limit audits to once a year, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, Vendor-borne cost (5% shortfall shift) and no direct system access; confirm nothing in Section 23 (records/assurance) creates a broader audit path.

No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee payable by Customer is stated; the closest exposure is the sec-2.1 take-or-pay shortfall (handled under MINCOMMIT). Note also that no SLA/service-credit regime appears in the body despite the credits reference in sec-1.5 and the service-level exhibit in sec-2.2.

sec-19.1–19.3 give services, conformity, malicious-code and compliance warranties with a 90-day Deliverable period and term-long hosted conformity; sec-19.4 provides repair/re-perform plus refund and termination, and is expressly non-exclusive for security, privacy and indemnified claims.

Insurance is present: CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M for the term plus one year, with certificates and non-limitation language in sec-18.2; check cyber limit against the health-data risk profile.

sec-2.1 imposes USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay for three years expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — remove or convert to a non-binding forecast, or at minimum add carry-forward, reduction on Vendor breach, and termination-linked release.

Section 10 addresses access wind-down, Deliverable delivery and refunds, but there is no express transition-assistance period or Customer Data export/return and deletion obligation; note Section 11 is referenced in sec-16.5 yet absent from the outline, so the data-return provisions may need to be added here.
